title: Data Residency and Evidence Matrix for Enterprise Evaluations
content:
Purpose:
This brief is a seller- and procurement-facing snapshot that maps common enterprise security controls (SOC2, ISO27001, HIPAA) to the artifacts and commitments Redwood can provide during an evaluation. The goal is to speed reviews by security teams and procurement, reduce back-and-forth, and give sellers short, defensible language for RFPs and SSO/contract conversations.

Executive summary (one paragraph):
Redwood Inference operates a production-first inference platform with documented controls and artifacts to satisfy SOC2 Type II, ISO27001-aligned posture, and HIPAA readiness for covered workloads. For procurement teams we provide: signed SOC2 Type II report (or SOC2 bridge letters for interim periods), ISO-aligned control descriptions and gap-closure roadmap, HIPAA BAAs and technical safeguards mapping, detailed data residency assurances (region-specific hosting and private deployment options), and an evidence matrix that ties common control asks to demonstrable artifacts (logs, configs, runbooks, contracts). Sellers should lead with: we offer hosted, dedicated, or private deployments to meet residency and isolation needs, we keep immutable audit logs with configurable retention, and we can provide tailored evidence packages during security reviews.

Audience and use cases:
- Security/assurance teams doing initial supplier risk assessments
- Procurement during RFP and contracting
- Seller/SE prep for technical deep dives and security demos
- Legal for BAA / DPA negotiations

Control-to-evidence mapping (high-level rows; use these as quick answers during calls):
1) Access controls (SOC2 CC6 / ISO A.9):
   - Evidence: IAM role listing, RBAC matrix export, SSO config screenshots (SAML metadata), MFA enforcement logs, quarterly access review runbook PDF.
   - Delivery options: Exported CSV + read-only access to a review account, or a recorded demo showing role creation and policy assignment.

2) Change management (SOC2 CC5 / ISO A.12.1):
   - Evidence: Git commit history for infra changes, PR review policy, CI job history, deploy runbook, change approval calendar entries.
   - Delivery: Link to auditable PRs (read-only) or sanitized diffs and a summary spreadsheet.

3) Logging & auditability (SOC2 CC7 / ISO A.12.4):
   - Evidence: Audit-log retention policy, sample anonymized log extracts, log pipeline diagram (where logs are stored and how they are retained), retention configuration per region.
   - Notes: For hosted API customers we offer per-customer audit packages; for Dedicated/Private customers logs can be routed to customer-managed SIEM.

4) Data residency & encryption (ISO A.10 / HIPAA Technical Safeguards):
   - Evidence: Data residency commitments (region list), KMS key rotation policy, encryption-at-rest screenshots, TLS configuration checks, key custody options (customer KMS/HSM integrations).
   - Seller line: "We can pin your tenant to a specific cloud region and support customer-managed keys for Dedicated and Private deployments."

5) Incident response & breach notification (SOC2 CC8 / ISO A.16):
   - Evidence: IR runbook, table-top exercise notes, incident timeline template, sample public post-mortem redaction, SLA for notification windows in contracts.

6) Third-party risk & supply chain (SOC2 / ISO A.15):
   - Evidence: Subprocessor list, up-to-date vendor assessments (questionnaire results), SOC2/ISO certifications of critical vendors where available.

7) HIPAA-specific controls (where customer workload is PHI):
   - Evidence: Signed BAA template, technical and administrative safeguard mapping doc (how Redwood meets HIPAA rules), options for on-prem/private deployment to minimize PHI exposure.

Competitive notes (short):
- Big cloud managed endpoints: often strong on certifications but lack inference-specific audit artifacts like per-model KV cache logs or prefix-caching behavior. Their data residency is typically region-limited but customers struggle with ephemeral multi-tenant inference logs.
- Open-source self-hosted stacks: good for control but heavy ops burden; customers trade vendor-managed evidence and speed-to-evaluate for internal engineering effort.
- Other LLM API providers: some will promise deletion policies and retention windows but lack transparent per-request audit trails or easy export of token-level cost/trace for e-discovery.

Redwood differentiator to emphasize in buyer conversations:
- Three deployment modes (hosted / dedicated / private) that map directly to procurement controls: we can move from "vendor-managed" (fast onboarding) to "customer-isolated" (contracted capacity) to "fully private" (air-gapped or VPC) without changing API surface.
- Evidence-as-a-service: pre-baked evidence bundles for SOC2/ISO initial assessments (artifact packages + one 60-min walkthrough) to accelerate security reviews.
- Audit log configurability: retention, anonymization options, and routing of raw logs to customer SIEM in dedicated/private modes.

Sample seller talking points (short snippets to use in calls or RFP responses):
- "We maintain SOC2 Type II controls audited annually; we can provide the report under NDA and a controls matrix linking to artifacts."
- "For customers needing PHI handling we sign a standard BAA and support Dedicated/Private deployments for minimized blast radius."
- "Audit logs are immutable, timestamped, and can be exported or streamed to your SIEM—we can provide a sample export and explain retention settings."
- "Data can be pinned to specific regions and we offer customer-managed KMS options for Dedicated and Private deployments."

Procurement & security FAQ (concise):
Q: Can you provide the SOC2 report?
A: Yes — SOC2 Type II is available under NDA. If a report window doesn't align, we provide a SOC2 bridge letter and an artifacts bundle.

Q: Will you sign a BAA?
A: Yes — we have a standard BAA. For high-risk PHI workloads we recommend Dedicated or Private deployment and a security review.

Q: Can logs be retained for X years?
A: Retention is configurable within platform limits; for longer legal holds we offer export workflows to customer storage.

Q: Where is customer data stored geographically?
A: We operate in multiple cloud regions; customers can pin tenancy to a region for Hosted + Dedicated or fully control location in Private. See region list in the evidence bundle.

Demo checklist for SE / seller before a security deep-dive call (quick):
- Pull latest SOC2 Type II report (or bridge letter) and ensure NDA template is ready.
- Prepare evidence bundle zip (control mapping table, sample logs, runbooks, screenshots).
- Confirm tenant/region to show in demo (use a sanitized demo tenant for PHI scenarios).
- Prepare IV/QA answers for: retention windows, KMS options, subprocessor list, and IR notification SLAs.

Potential sensitive asks & recommended responses (tough procurement questions):
- "Can you guarantee deletion of all derived embeddings or model cache entries?"
  - Recommended: Be specific about retention settings and technical limits; offer Dedicated or Private deployment for full data isolation and customer-managed cache policies.
- "We need continuous network-level packet capture for audit."
  - Recommended: Offer hosted packet-level evidence only for Dedicated/Private via customer-managed monitoring integration; explain the security and privacy trade-offs.

Next steps / action items for this doc (owner: Maya Chen):
- Create a ready-to-send evidence bundle template (zip) that includes: controls matrix, redacted SOC2 report, sample logs, runbooks, region list, BAA template. Target date: 2026-03-24.
- Draft two short one-pagers for sellers: "Security one-pager for procurement" and "Technical evidence checklist for SEs". Target: 2026-03-17.
- Coordinate with Security to validate the control mapping and add definitive links to artifacts in Confluence (SEC team to provide canonical URLs).

Notes / open questions (for security & legal):
- Confirm which versions of the SOC2 report we can reliably share under NDA and whether redacted versions are fine for first-pass evals.
- Finalize maximum retention we can promise in hosted mode without a Dedicated contract.
- Decide how we standardize anonymized log extracts for demos to avoid accidental exposure of customer data.

Appendix: quick snippets for RFP responses (copyable):
- "SOC2: Redwood Inference maintains SOC2 Type II controls audited by an independent assessor. Report available under NDA. Controls matrix provided upon request."
- "HIPAA: Redwood will execute a BAA and supports Dedicated/Private deployment for PHI workloads; technical safeguards and encryption controls are documented in our HIPAA readiness package."
- "Data residency: We support region-specific tenancy and customer KMS options for Dedicated and Private deployments; see region list in evidence bundle."

End of brief.
